checklist.feature: Three-storey red-brick wings and overall courtyard footprint
Prominent front-facing gables of differing scale
Gabled roof features along the long wings
Dormers embedded in the roof slopes
Deep window surrounds and articulated façade bays

defects: Broad, relatively plain roof planes suppress the reference’s complex roof silhouette despite the strong overall outline match.
The two front gables read as similar repeated modules rather than the more varied, prominent gables in the reference.
Several dormers read as small boxes placed on the roof rather than openings integrated into its slopes.
Flat, uniformly repeated windows and horizontal bands replace the reference’s substantial window-surround and bay relief.
Pointed roof elements look mechanically repeated; some have abrupt cylindrical bases.
fixes: Rebuild the roof kit with distinct intersecting steep roof volumes, resolved valleys, and legible changes of plane at the courtyard corner.
Give the principal front gable its own larger profile and placement; vary the secondary gables to match the reference rather than duplicating one module.
Cut dormer openings into the roof planes and join their sidewalls and miniature roofs cleanly to the surrounding slopes.
Add a window-surround kit with recessed glazing, projecting pale trim, lintels, and stronger bay-to-bay depth where supported by the reference.
Vary the pointed corner-feature kit by location and blend its bases into the adjacent roof geometry.
Replace the conspicuous uniform roof pattern and flat brick fill with subtler, finer-scale material texture.
keep: The broadly matching wing layout and three-storey massing.
The red masonry, pale trim, and slate-coloured roof material separation.
The established window rhythm and roof chimney distribution.
